[anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-other] We found that high-quality constitutional documents combined with fictional stories portraying an aligned AI can reduce agentic misalignment by more than a factor of three despite being unrelated to the evaluation scenario.
[anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-other] We evaluated these models over the run on agentic misalignment evals, constitution adherence evals, and our automated alignment assessment.
[anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-other] Discussion Agentic misalignment was one of the first major alignment failures we found in our models and required establishing new mitigation processes—ones that have since become standard for us.

[anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-other] Full-text excerpt:
When we first published this research, our most capable frontier models were from the Claude 4 family. This was also the first model family for which we ran a live alignment assessment during training;1 agentic misalignment was one of several behavioral issues that surfaced. Thus, after Claude 4, it was clear we needed to improve our safety training and, since then, we have made significant updates to our safety training.
Footnote 2: Sonnet 4.5 scored well under 1%, but not quite 0; Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Mythos preview, and Opus 4.7 all score 0. The results on more recent models may be confounded by the presence of information about the evaluation in the pre-training corpus.
